# Solid-Earth body tide (IERS 2010), computed by Craton

`iers_tides` · adapter 1.0.0 · makes `solid_earth_tide` tokens

| | |
|---|---|
| Provider | Computed locally by `craton.geo.solid_tide` |
| Home | https://iers-conventions.obspm.fr/chapter7.php |
| Licence | `CC-BY-4.0` |

## Terms

Computed values. Tokens at earthquakes inherit the catalogue's CC-BY-4.0 (their positions and times are INGV's); the hourly series is computed from nothing but the clock and is offered under the same licence for simplicity. The code is a derived work of the IERS Conventions software and carries its notice (`craton/geo/IERS_NOTICE.txt`).

## Cite

- Petit, G. and Luzum, B. (eds.) (2010). IERS Conventions (2010). IERS Technical Note 36, chapter 7.1.1. Verlag des Bundesamts für Kartographie und Geodäsie.
- Mathews, P. M., Dehant, V. and Gipson, J. M. (1997). Tidal station displacements. J. Geophys. Res. 102(B9), 20469-20477.
- Montenbruck, O. and Gill, E. (2000). Satellite Orbits: Models, Methods and Applications. Springer. Section 3.3.2 (Sun and Moon).

## Access

Nothing is downloaded. Event positions come from the `ingv_catalog` tokens of the same build; the Sun and the Moon come from analytic series.

## From the source to the token

| Token slot | Comes from |
|---|---|
| `kind` | `forcing` |
| `lat, lon` | the event's epicentre, or the centre of the region's box |
| `depth_km` | 0: the displacement of the ellipsoid surface at that point |
| `time` | the event's origin time, or every hour on the hour |
| `value` | east, north, up displacement, metres, rounded to 1 µm |
| `qualifiers` | model = IERS2010 |
| `provenance.record` | `event=<EventID>` or `hourly=centre` |
| `provenance.content_hash` | the event token's hash, or the hash of the request (place, time, model) |

## Uncertainty

1 mm per channel (`derived`): the largest difference from the same model driven by the JPL DE440 ephemeris is 0.71 mm, and from PySolid 0.4 mm, over six places from 1990 to 2026 (`tests/test_solid_tide.py`).

## Known issues

- Displacement, not stress. Whether a tide pushes a fault towards failure depends on the fault's orientation; a tidal-stress instrument can come later.
- Body tide only: ocean loading (a few mm to cm inland, more on coasts) and pole tide are not included.
- Earth rotation is approximated by mean sidereal time with UT1 = UTC; the error is far below a millimetre.
- The permanent tide is kept (the IERS 'conventional tide free' convention).
